auth.description: Dropbox access token sent as a bearer — a scoped app access token or an OAuth2 access token
auth.name: dropbox.access_token
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: Create an app at dropbox.com/developers/apps. For a quick connection, generate an access token directly from the app's Settings tab. For a token that keeps working for other users, complete the app's OAuth2 authorization flow and supply the resulting access token
config.label: Access token
config.name: access_token

description: Dropbox: browse folder contents, read file and folder metadata, search files, create folders, and get temporary download links

operations.description: Get the account this access token authenticates as, confirming the token resolves and naming the account it belongs to. Takes no parameters. Dropbox routes this read through POST, like every operation this connector declares — there is no GET anywhere in Dropbox's v2 API

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, if known

operations.description: List the files and folders directly inside a folder, first page only. Each entry names its own type (file, folder, or deleted), name and full path. Direction remains conservatively authored as write pending individual review; POST is transport only and supplied no evidence

params.description: The full path of the folder to list, from the account root — or the empty string "" for the root folder itself. Dropbox's root has no other spelling: "/" is a documented error (path/not_found or path/malformed_path), not an alias for ""
params.name: path

cursor.description: The cursor for continuing to the next page. This connector cannot fetch it — list_folder/continue is not shipped

entries.description: This page's items, each {".tag": "file"|"folder"|"deleted", name, path_lower, path_display, id}

has_more.description: True when the folder holds more entries than this page returned. This connector cannot fetch them; see cursor

operations.description: Get metadata for a file or folder at a given path: its type, name, id, and — for a file — size and content hash. Does not return a folder's contents (use dropbox-folder-list) or a file's content (use dropbox-temporary-link-get). Direction remains conservatively authored as write pending individual review; POST is transport only and supplied no evidence

params.description: The full path of the file or folder to inspect, from the account root. Unlike dropbox-folder-list, the account root itself ("") is not addressable this way — this path must name an existing file or folder
params.name: path

.tag.description: "file", "folder" or "deleted" — which fields below apply depends on this

client_modified.description: File only: the modification time the uploading client claimed, not verified by Dropbox

content_hash.description: File only: Dropbox's own content hash, for verifying a download performed some other way

id.description: An opaque id stable across moves and renames

rev.description: File only: an opaque revision id

server_modified.description: File only: when Dropbox's server last saw this content change

operations.description: Search file and folder names across the account, returning the first page of matches. Dropbox matches on name, not file content. Direction remains conservatively authored as write pending individual review; POST is transport only and supplied no evidence

params.description: The text to match against file and folder names
params.name: query

cursor.description: The cursor for the next page, present only when has_more is true. Unusable here, for the reason given on has_more

has_more.description: True when more matches exist than this page returned. This connector cannot fetch them — no continuation cursor is shipped

matches.description: The matching files and folders, each {metadata: {...}, match_type: {".tag": "filename"|"content"|"both"}}

operations.description: Create a new folder at the given path, including any missing parent folders. Naming a path that already exists answers 409 conflict rather than creating a duplicate, since autorename is not offered by this connector

params.description: The full path of the new folder, from the account root, e.g. "/Homework/math". Dropbox creates any missing parent folders along the way
params.name: path

metadata.description: The created folder's metadata: {name, path_lower, path_display, id}

id.description: The created folder's id — what a later call addresses it by

operations.description: Get a temporary, unauthenticated download link for an existing file's content, valid for approximately four hours. This connector cannot follow the link itself — it only returns the URL, for a caller to fetch separately. Direction remains conservatively authored as write pending individual review; POST is transport only and supplied no evidence

params.description: The full path of the file to link, from the account root. Must name a file, not a folder
params.name: path

link.description: The temporary download URL, valid for approximately four hours from this call

metadata.description: The linked file's metadata, the same shape dropbox-metadata-get returns for a file
